final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

comments.body:
Done — all three questions answered, report attached.

**Short version:** hybrid. DIY the leash pulling (it's mechanics, 10 min/day, free). Pay for the reactivity, because it needs a decoy dog at a controlled distance and you can't arrange that on a public trail. Total ~$150–395 instead of $1,200–2,800.

**Best local option:** Orion Dog Training, San Jose — $395 for a 6-week reactivity-specific class, small group (4–5 teams), Saturday 5:30pm cohort fits your availability. Free 20-min consult first, 650-996-6708. Cheaper fallback is Santa Clara Dog Training Club at $150/7 weeks, but it's general obedience and Tuesday 4/5pm may not clear your workday. I ruled out one heavily-marketed option because it's e-collar based, which is the wrong tool for a fear/arousal reactive dog.

**Four-week plan** is in the report — the key structural point is that you train the pulling and the reactivity *separately* for the first two weeks, and everything in the reactivity track keys off one number: his threshold distance. That's why "find the threshold distance" is its own subtask; do it before week 2.

Two things I couldn't settle for you: whether the Tuesday 5pm class time actually works with your schedule, and whether Orion's next cohort after Aug 28 lands somewhere you can attend. Both are answered by the phone call, which is subtask 1.

Setting this to `needs_review` — five subtasks are yours, the first three are worth doing this week since the Santa Clara club's Aug 11 session and its refund deadline are close.

report.markdown:
> **Note:** Prices and class dates below were pulled from the trainers' own pages in Aug 2026. Anything with a start date should be reconfirmed by phone before you pay.

# Training plan — 14-month rescue border collie mix, South Bay

## 1. Trainer or DIY? → Do both, cheaply

**Hire for the reactivity, DIY the pulling.**

Loose-leash walking is a mechanics-and-consistency problem. It responds to 10 minutes a day in your driveway and costs nothing. You do not need to pay someone $1,500 to teach you to stop walking when the leash goes tight.

Barking at every dog is different. Fixing it requires another dog at a **known, controlled distance** that stays there. You cannot manufacture that on a public trail — every dog that appears is too close, and each incident rehearses the behaviour rather than changing it. Buying access to controlled setups is the whole value of a class here.

Also relevant: 14 months is an adolescent border collie. Highly trainable, but this is the window where reactive habits calcify. Not a wait-and-see situation.

**Budget:** $150–$395 total, versus $1,200–$2,800 for a full private package.

**One hard rule:** avoid e-collar / prong / "balanced" programs for this dog. Punishing a bark that comes from arousal or fear can suppress the warning while leaving the feeling intact. This rules out one of the most heavily marketed local options.

**Escalate to private 1:1 (~$150/hr) only if:** he won't take food within ~100 ft of another dog, he redirects onto you or the leash, or he has bitten.

---

## 2. Local options with real prices

| Option | Price | Format | When / where | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Orion Dog Training** — "My dog is reactive, now what?" | **$395** | 6-week class, 4–5 teams, 3,000 sq ft indoor, homework w/ videos | Sat 5:30pm and Fri 1pm cohorts; next start Aug 28. 576 E Santa Clara St, San Jose | **Best fit.** Reactivity-specific, force-free, small group, weekend slot |
| **Santa Clara Dog Training Club** — Beginning/Intermediate Obedience | **$150** + $2.50 reg. | 7-week group class | Tuesdays 4pm or 5pm; next session starts Aug 11, 2026. 344 Tully Rd, San Jose | **Cheapest.** General obedience, not reactivity curriculum. Weekday afternoon may not work |
| **Lori Hamilton Dog Training** — private package | **$1,500** / 10 points ($150 per point) | 1:1, flexible point system, campus or nearby park | San Jose | Only if you want pure 1:1 |
| ~~Off Leash K9 San Jose~~ | $1,400 (8-lesson reactivity) or $500 first lesson then $100/session | Private, e-collar based | San Jose | **Ruled out** — remote-collar program |

**Contact:** Orion — text/call 650-996-6708, oriondogtraining@gmail.com. Offers a **free 20-minute phone consult** and asks you to contact them before enrolling to confirm fit. Santa Clara club registers via `santa-clara-dog-training-club.coursestorm.com`.

Note the Santa Clara club refund window closes the day before the first class.

---

## 3. The first four weeks

**Equipment:** 5–6 ft flat leash, front-clip harness, pea-sized high-value treats (string cheese, hot dog, freeze-dried liver), waist treat pouch. No retractable leash. No prong or e-collar.

**Time:** 10–15 min on weekday evenings, one 30-min weekend session. Short and frequent beats long and occasional.

**The core principle:** train the two problems *separately* for the first two weeks. Never work loose-leash skills in the presence of other dogs until the mechanics are automatic in a boring environment.

### Week 1 — Foundations, zero other dogs

- **Weekday evenings (10 min):** Charge a marker word. Say "yes," feed a treat. 20 reps. Then in your driveway or hallway: walk 3 steps, mark and feed while the leash is slack. The instant the leash tightens, **stop moving** and stand still. When he releases the tension, mark, feed, walk on. He learns pulling stops progress.
- **One weekend session (30 min):** Find his threshold distance. Park where you can see dog traffic from far away. Identify the distance at which he *notices* another dog but will still eat from your hand. **Write that number down.** Weeks 2–4 depend on it.
- **Management this week:** walk at low-traffic hours — early morning, late evening. Every avoided incident is a win. Two or three good 15-min sniff walks beat one stressful 45-min one.
- **Success looks like:** 10 slack-leash steps in the driveway, and a known threshold number.

### Week 2 — Add the U-turn and start counter-conditioning

- **Weekday (10 min):** Emergency U-turn. Say a cue ("this way!"), turn 180°, jog 3 steps, feed lavishly. 10 reps per session, no dogs present. This becomes your escape hatch for the next two years.
- **Weekend (30 min):** "Look at That." At or *beyond* your threshold distance, the moment he sees a dog, mark and feed. Dog appears → chicken happens. You are not asking for obedience, you are changing what another dog predicts. If he can't eat, you're too close — back up 20 ft immediately.
- **Success looks like:** the U-turn works on cue with no dog present; he can look at a distant dog and turn back to you for food.

### Week 3 — Move the mechanics outdoors, hold the distance

- **Weekday (15 min):** Loose-leash work on a quiet sidewalk instead of the driveway. Same stop-when-tight rule. Add turns and pace changes so he has to track you.
- **Weekend (30 min):** Same Look-at-That game, same distance. **Do not close the gap yet.** Add "Catch 1-2-3": count out loud, feed on 3, as a portable pattern that pulls his attention off a trigger.
- **Success looks like:** he can walk a quiet block on a slack leash; he offers a check-in when he spots a dog instead of fixating.

### Week 4 — Close the distance slightly, then reassess

- **Weekday (15 min):** Alternate loose-leash walking with U-turn reps. Practise on a slightly busier route, still using distance and U-turns to stay under threshold.
- **Weekend (30 min):** Reduce working distance by roughly 20%. If you get two reactions in one session, go back to the previous distance for another week. Progress is not linear and repeating a week is normal.
- **End of week 4:** review your log and decide — continue solo, or start the class.

### What "good" looks like at the end of week 4

Not a dog who ignores other dogs. A dog who *notices* one, glances at you, and can be walked away. Full reactivity work usually takes 3–6 months; four weeks buys you the foundation and a dog whose walks are no longer unpleasant.

### Border-collie-specific note

Under-exercised herding brains are more reactive. Pair this with 10 minutes of daily sniffing work or a food puzzle — mental work tires him more than distance walking and lowers his baseline arousal, which makes every session above go better.

---

## What to do next

1. Text Orion at 650-996-6708 to book the free consult *(15 min)*
2. Decide Orion $395 vs Santa Clara $150 *(15 min)*
3. Buy harness + treats before Week 1 *(30 min, ~$60-80)*
4. Run the Week 1 weekend session to find the threshold distance
5. Keep a one-line daily log

All five are live subtasks on this task.

subtasks.title: Decide: DIY vs hire a trainer for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description:
RECOMMENDATION: Hybrid — do the daily work yourself, but buy ONE structured reactivity course to get coached.

Reasoning:
- Leash pulling alone is a clean DIY project. A 14-month border collie mix is smart, food/motion-motivated, and loose-leash walking is mostly mechanics + consistency, 10 min/day.
- Reactive barking at every dog is the part that goes wrong DIY. It needs controlled setups with a neutral "decoy" dog at a known distance, which you cannot arrange on a public South Bay trail — every dog that appears is at the wrong distance and you end up rehearsing the reaction instead of fixing it. That is the single thing a class or trainer buys you.
- 14 months = adolescent border collie. Behaviour is fully changeable but this is the window where habits harden. Not a "wait and see" case.
- Cost of the hybrid: ~$150-$395 total, vs $1,200-$2,800 for full private packages.

DO NOT: use e-collar / "balanced" programs for a reactive dog. Punishing the bark can suppress the warning and worsen the underlying arousal. Rules out the cheapest-looking aggressive-marketing options (see sibling task).

Escalate to 1:1 private ($150-250/hr) only if: dog can't take food within 100ft of another dog, redirects onto you/leash, or has bitten.

subtasks.title: Write week-by-week 4-week training plan (evenings + weekends)
subtasks.description: 4-week plan written; full version in the report on the parent task. Structure: two separate tracks trained separately — (A) loose-leash mechanics in low-distraction settings, (B) distance-based counter-conditioning to other dogs. Never train both at once in week 1-2. 10-15 min on weekday evenings, one 30-min weekend session. Equipment: 5-6ft flat leash + front-clip harness (no retractable, no prong/e-collar), high-value soft treats cut small, treat pouch.

subtasks.title: Text Orion Dog Training to book the free 20-min consult
subtasks.description: Text or call 650-996-6708 (or email oriondogtraining@gmail.com) to book the free 20-minute phone consult for the 'My dog is reactive, now what?' 6-week class, $395. They explicitly ask you to contact them before signing up to check fit. Say: 14-month rescue border collie mix, barks/lunges at other dogs on leash, pulls hard, available evenings and weekends. Ask: (1) is the Sat 5:30pm cohort open, (2) next start date after Aug 28, (3) is a decoy/neutral dog used and at what distance, (4) refund policy if he can't cope in week 1.

subtasks.title: Decide: Orion $395 reactivity class vs Santa Clara club $150 obedience class
subtasks.description: Pick one after the Orion consult. Orion = reactivity-specific, small group, weekend slot, $395. Santa Clara Dog Training Club = $150 + $2.50, 7 weeks, Tuesdays 4/5pm, general obedience only, next start Aug 11 2026 (register at santa-clara-dog-training-club.coursestorm.com). If the Tuesday time doesn't clear work, Orion is the answer by default.

subtasks.title: Buy a front-clip harness and high-value treats before Week 1
subtasks.description: Needed to start the DIY plan. 5-6ft flat leash (no retractable), front-clip / no-pull harness fitted to a medium border collie mix, soft high-value treats cut into pea-size pieces (string cheese, hot dog, or freeze-dried liver), and a treat pouch that clips to your waist. Do NOT buy a prong or e-collar. ~$60-80 total.

subtasks.title: Find your dog's threshold distance (Week 1 weekend session)
subtasks.description: One 20-30 min session. Park where you can see a sidewalk with dog traffic but stay far from it. Note the distance at which your dog notices another dog but will still take a treat from you. That number is your working distance for weeks 1-4 — write it in this description once you have it. Everything else in the reactivity track depends on it.

subtasks.title: Log progress daily for 4 weeks (one line per day)
subtasks.description: One line per session: date, what you trained, threshold distance, number of reactions, how it felt. Phone notes app is fine. This is the data you bring to the trainer and the only way you'll notice slow improvement. Review at the end of week 4 and decide whether to continue solo or escalate to private 1:1 (~$150/session).
